chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Umar, from Aban, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'If you marry a woman for a month, do you keep back a portion of her from yourself?' He said, 'Yes, take from her in proportion to what she is withheld from you; if it is half the month, then half, and if it is a third, then a third.'

And whenever he gives her something of the dowry, then it becomes clear that she has a husband, she is entitled to what she took, in exchange for what he legalized of her private part, and he is not obliged to give her what remained of the dowry upon him.

key_terms.أَبَانٍ: Aban, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature.
key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّ: To legalize or make permissible, specifically referring to the right of conjugal use.
key_terms.الْمَهْرِ: The dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife.
key_terms.عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ: Umar ibn Hanzalah, a key narrator often cited in hadiths from the Imams.
key_terms.فَرْجِهَا: Her private part, referring to the marital right of intimacy.

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for temporary marriage duration and dowry payment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the proportional allocation of the dowry (mahr) in temporary marriage (mut'ah), establishing that the husband retains the portion corresponding to the duration of the contract. It further distinguishes the legal status of the dowry if the woman was already married, noting that the paid amount serves as compensation for the 'permissibility' of her body during that period, relieving the husband of any remaining balance. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view of mut'ah as a distinct contractual relationship with specific financial and temporal boundaries.
